objectives: Identify rimes in taught fl-words and familiar CVC partners.
Group words that share the vowel and ending sounds.
Distinguish words that share fl but have different rimes.
Decode each word fully after sorting.
concepts: A word family shares a rime, not necessarily an onset.
Fl-words such as flap, flip, flop, flag and flat have different rimes.
CVC partners such as cap, lip, top, bag and cat make the rime pattern visible.
Word-family sorting supports decoding but does not replace it.

definitions.definition: Words that share a rime, such as flap and cap with -ap.
The vowel and sounds that follow it in a syllable.
The initial consonant sound or group before the vowel.

workedExamples.solution: They share -ap; flap has onset fl and cap has onset c.
Both begin fl but have different rimes: -ag and -at.

commonMistakes: Grouping words by onset instead of rime.
Treating all fl-words as one family.
Ignoring the final consonant when sorting.
Guessing from the family label rather than decoding the full word.
keyTakeaways: Compare the vowel and ending to identify a rime.
Words with the same onset can have different rimes.
Words with different onsets can share a rime.
Decode the whole word after sorting.
revisionPoints: flag and bag share -ag; flat and cat share -at.

basic.prompt: What is the rime in flip?

conceptual.prompt: What makes flap and cap a word-family pair?
Do flag and flat share a rime?
conceptual.answer: No; flag has -ag and flat has -at.

conceptual.prompt: Why should you decode after sorting?
conceptual.answer: The family pattern helps but does not replace reading the whole word.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are flag and bag alike and different?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They share -ag; flag has onset fl and bag has onset b.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why are flap and flip in different rime groups?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Their vowel and ending differ: -ap and -ip.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: What should you do if a word does not sound like its family?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Decode it again and check every grapheme.

mixedReview.prompt: What is the onset in flop?
What does a word-family sort help you notice?
mixedReview.answer: Shared rimes and differences among words

activities.name: Sort fl-words by rime.
steps: Read flap, flip, flop, flag and flat.
Pair each with a familiar CVC word sharing its rime.
Name the onset and rime in each word.
Read every word again to confirm the sort.

activities.name: Compare fl-words with similar rimes.
steps: Contrast flag/flat to hear the ending difference.
Explain why the onset alone cannot identify the word.

outcomes: Identify onset and rime in taught fl-words.
Explain differences among fl-words with the same onset.
Decode the full word after sorting.
